display.purpose: Brand-site hero only. Space Grotesk, tight and luminous, one per page.

app-body.purpose: Product-app default text (Geist). Denser, tuned for tables and forms.

mono.purpose: Machine-addressable text only: brain IDs, MCP URLs, tokens, code (JetBrains Mono).

shadows.name: inset-highlight
shadows.purpose: Default resting treatment on app-surface / surface-card — a single bright top edge, not a drop shadow.

shadows.name: accent-ring
shadows.purpose: Barely-there accent-tinted outline keeping surfaces in the purple family.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Ambient shadow for elements that leave the plane: dialogs, popovers, dropdowns, toasts, and hover-lift.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: Default exponential ease-out for entrances and state transitions. No bounce, no elastic.

motion.name: beam-flow
motion.purpose: Dashed synaptic links flowing along the brain network.

motion.name: node-pulse
motion.purpose: Brain network nodes pulsing in opacity and scale.

narrative.overview: Context101 looks like a powered-on brain in a dark room. Near-black substrate, signal moving along faint magenta-violet traces, light pooling only where there's activity. The identity is unapologetically dark and unapologetically purple: the --brain mark is the loudest thing on the page, and that's the point. The system spans two surfaces that are recognizably the same product — a drenched-dark brand site (site/) built on Space Grotesk + Inter, and a quieter, instrumented product app (web/) on Geist with a light-default magenta-tinted OKLCH palette. Brand can shout; product keeps its voice down. The shared --brain purple is the thread between them. It rejects corporate-cold sterility and enterprise-heavy clutter alike.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, purple, and committed to it — the brand mark leads, it doesn't hide
Two registers, one identity: drenched-dark brand site, quiet light-default product app, shared accent
Confident & tactile components — surfaces that lift, buttons that press, motion that rewards
Depth is hybrid: flat at rest, real shadow only on things that float
Engineer-grade legibility over decoration; honest state over fake progress

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one brand color: the brain purple. Magenta and violet are two stops of the same identity, not separate roles. The only non-purple color permitted is destructive red, and only on destructive/error affordances.

rules.name: The Tinted-Gray Rule
rules.body: No gray is neutral. Every background, border, and muted text value carries chroma toward hue ~320-328. A truly desaturated gray is forbidden — it reads cold and breaks the family.

rules.name: The Display-Stays-Home Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk display sizes live on the brand site. The product app earns hierarchy through weight, size, and spacing on Geist, not by importing the marketing voice.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for things a machine reads or addresses: brain IDs, MCP URLs, bearer tokens, connector keys, code. Never decorative emphasis.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-It-Floats Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces get tonal layering, an inset highlight, and an accent-tinted border — never an ambient drop shadow. Drop shadows appear only on elements that leave the plane: overlays, and the hover/active lift of tactile components.

dos: Do lead with the brain purple. It's the one accent — primary actions, active states, focus rings, the brand mark.
Do tint every neutral toward hue ~320-328 so the product reads as the brand at low volume.
Do keep the brand site dark and drenched and the product app quiet (light-default OKLCH, with .dark). Same identity, two volumes.
Do convey resting depth with tonal layering, an inset highlight, and an accent-tinted border. Save real drop shadows for things that float.
Do make components tactile: hover lifts, active presses, focus shows a visible accent ring.
Do use JetBrains Mono for anything machine-addressable — brain IDs, MCP endpoints, tokens, code.
Do keep prefers-reduced-motion alternatives on every animation, and keep the synaptic beams aria-hidden and non-blocking.
Do show honest state. Pending / ingesting / ready / failed must each be visibly distinct — no silent failures, no fake progress.
donts: Don't go corporate-cold. No navy-and-gray fintech sterility, no stock photography, no soulless enterprise polish.
Don't go enterprise-heavy. No AWS-console density, no walls of gray tables dumped on the user.
Don't use a truly desaturated gray anywhere — it reads cold and breaks the purple family.
Don't introduce a second decorative accent hue. Destructive red is the only non-purple color, and only on destructive/error affordances.
Don't put Space Grotesk display type in the product app.
Don't drop an ambient shadow on a resting surface — that's the 2014 tell.
Don't nest a card inside a card. Ever.

Don't ship the cross-register AI tells: gradient text, side-stripe borders, decorative glassmorphism, the hero-metric template, identical icon-card grids, or tracked-uppercase eyebrows above every section.
Don't let muted or placeholder text fall below 4.5:1 against its background, especially the dusty-lilac muted on dark.
